deck_title: Blinn halfway-vector microfacet bisector vs Phong mirror double-angle cutoff rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic James Blinn (SIGGRAPH 1977) halfway-vector microfacet cosine evaluation (H = normalize(L + V), N*H = cos(theta_h) > 0 across all theta_h in [0, 90 deg)) versus Bui Tuong Phong (1975) mirror-reflection dot product (max(0, R*V) = max(0, cos(2*theta_h)) = max(0, 2*mu_h^2 - 1), which clips to 0.0000 for all theta_h >= 45 deg) and 64-substep geodesic angular bisector arc integration across 17 microfacet tilt stations (mu_h in [1.0000, 0.2000]).

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: All physically based microfacet BRDFs (Blinn SIGGRAPH 1977 / Cook-Torrance / GGX) where specular reflection occurs on microfacets aligned with H = normalize(L+V)
Headlight, camera-flash, and grazing wet-road specular highlights that must not suffer a hard circular cutoff at theta_h = 45 deg
Eliminating the R = 2(N*L)N - L reflection vector double-angle sign flip when 2*theta_h > 90 deg
Direct vector bisector dot product replacing 64-substep geodesic arc bisection
not_for: Perfect delta-mirror ray tracing on a zero-roughness plane (where only theta_h = 0 reflects)
